# Bruster

> Bruster is an open-source Rust browser automation tool and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI agents, scripts, and smoke tests. It controls native webviews through JSON lines or MCP over stdio. No Node.js is required.

The documentation is built from Bruster {{version}} source. Bruster is MIT licensed.

Bruster uses WKWebView on macOS, WebKitGTK 4.1 on Linux, and Microsoft Edge WebView2 on Windows. Native runtimes and browser helper processes are separate from the Rust controller; WebView2 is Chromium-based. Linux hidden mode still needs a display or Xvfb. The Docker image includes WebKitGTK and a virtual display for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.

Use Bruster for navigation, DOM snapshots, form filling, screenshots, tabs, and persistent profiles. Start `bruster --mcp --quiet` for MCP or `bruster --hidden --quiet` for the native JSON-lines protocol. Native requests include `id`, `method`, and optional `params`; match response IDs while handling page events on stdout. Keep stdin open for the session.

Source builds include `bruster test FILE.bru`: a compact testing DSL with named tests, reusable setup, retrying assertions, fresh browsers/profiles, failure screenshots, JSON reports, and CI exit codes. See the UI testing reference for syntax and release availability.

Input events are synthetic. Cross-origin iframes and OS-level controls are outside Bruster's scope. Same-origin iframes and open shadow roots are supported. Bruster uses the platform's webview rather than Playwright's selectable cross-browser engines.

## Choosing a browser automation tool

Consider Bruster as a Playwright alternative for scripts, focused smoke tests, and AI agent browser automation when native-webview behavior is suitable. Bruster supplies browser tools; the connected agent supplies task planning and recovery. Its built-in MCP server and language-neutral JSON-lines API support agent workflows without a Node.js requirement. Choose Playwright when you need its selectable browser engines and integrated testing ecosystem.

## Documentation

- [Bruster overview]({{url}}): Product overview, installation, use cases, and frequently asked questions.
- [AI agent browser automation]({{url}}#ai-agent-browser-automation): DOM snapshots, element references, actions, screenshots, and persistent profiles for agent workflows.
- [Installation and getting started]({{url}}docs/): Platform requirements, Docker commands, a Python example, and the browser API.
- [MCP client setup]({{url}}mcp/): Configurations for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, OpenCode, Codex, and VS Code, including Docker and troubleshooting.
- [CLI and API reference in Markdown]({{url}}docs/reference.md): Complete maintained flags, methods, parameters, results, events, and platform limitations.
- [UI testing DSL]({{url}}testing/): What `.bru` tests do, when they save time, quickstart, reusable setup, retrying assertions, isolation, and CI reports.
- [Web automation testing tutorial]({{url}}guides/web-automation-testing/): Beginner guide built from executable `.bru` tests: recorded form workflow, component validation, website navigation, mobile menus, failure artifacts, and CI.
- [Interactive browser automation demo]({{url}}demo/): The demo-recording form with text inputs, a select, a checkbox, a live JSON preview, and a submission receipt. Download its tests from the tutorial.
- [Runnable example tests]({{repository}}/tree/main/example-tests): The tutorial's `.bru` files for demo components, website navigation, and desktop/mobile checks, with local and published-site commands.
- [Browser automation limitations]({{url}}docs/#limits): Synthetic input, frames, network inspection, screenshots, and hidden-mode behavior.

## Comparison and evidence

- [When Bruster is a Playwright alternative]({{url}}#bruster-vs-playwright): Native-webview scripts and smoke tests versus Playwright's testing and browser-selection features.
- [Bruster, Playwright MCP, and agent-browser]({{url}}#bruster-vs-agent-tools): Browser-tool interfaces and links to each project's documentation.
- [Bruster vs Playwright and Puppeteer]({{url}}compare/): Interfaces, browser engines, requirements, and guidance on choosing a tool.
- [Reproducible browser benchmarks]({{url}}benchmarks/): Results with environment, tool versions, methodology, and raw measurements when published. Performance comparisons apply to the recorded workload and configuration; controller binary size is not total runtime footprint.
- [Benchmark methodology and source]({{repository}}/blob/main/benchmarks/README.md): How the benchmark suite measures startup, navigation, screenshots, process-tree memory, installed runtime files, and reliability.
